content: Make agent-created Git commits use the active agent harness as both Author and Committer without overwriting the repository user's Git identity, and prove the rule through the start-work skill and an isolated commit fixture.

Agent-created content, checkpoint, and closing-record commits use a command-local harness identity through start-work; human Git configuration remains unchanged, and the pre-commit hook remains a validator rather than an agent-identity detector.

Added the Codex and Claude Code harness mappings, environment detection, protected-option rejection, and an isolated seven-case forward test; both workflow skills passed package validation, Agent records and skill routing passed, and content revision ded1dad4172b515a3b17cb66c3f7aa18df9cb20e recorded Codex as both Author and Committer while local Git configuration remained amamiya.

Merge, revert, and cherry-pick results that need a new agent commit are prepared with no-commit mode and finalized through the helper; fast-forwards preserve their existing commit identity. Conservative short-option parsing rejects attached c or C tokens, while the documented separated -m form remains supported.
